Orange Alert for Nagarkurnool District from Nov 2 (8:30 AM) to Nov 3 (8:30 AM). Yellow Alert on Nov 3 & 4.
Hyderabad: Nagarkurnool District Collector Hemanta Keshav Patil has urged residents to follow India Meteorological Department (IMD) advisories and take necessary precautions as an orange alert has been issued for Nagarkurnool district from 8.30 am on November 2 to 8.30 am on November 3.
Heavy to very heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds are likely during this period, with wind speeds expected to reach 60–90 kmph. A yellow alert has also been issued for November 3 and 4.
Residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel, stay away from trees, electric poles and hoardings, and avoid open areas during lightning. People living in low-lying areas have been asked to remain alert, while livestock should be kept in safe places.
In case of emergencies, residents can contact the district helpline at 9866756825.

articles.full_text:
Cyclone Murasu Telangana | Hyderabad, Nov 2: Weather experts say Cyclone Murasu, which has strengthened in the Bay of Bengal, will have a strong impact on Telangana.
Heavy rain is likely in several parts of south Telangana on November 3, 4 and 5, with dense cloud and cold winds. The source says reports with 95 per cent confidence point to this.
The cyclone’s impact is expected to peak from the afternoon of November 3 to midnight on November 4. Officials said Nalgonda, Nagarkurnool, Suryapet and Wanaparthy districts may receive about 100 to 130 mm of rain. The weather department has already issued an orange alert for these districts. Officials are on alert because low-lying areas face the risk of flooding.
Cyclone Murasu Telangana | Forecast for Hyderabad and north Telangana
Hyderabad and surrounding districts may get moderate rain, while north Telangana is likely to see light showers. Today, November 2, moderate rain is expected in east, south and central Telangana, and light rain elsewhere.
The cyclone’s effect is expected to weaken gradually, and rain is likely to reduce significantly across the state after November 6. Thunder, lightning and gusty winds may hit over the next three days.
Disaster management officials have asked farmers to move their produce to safe places. They have also advised people to take precautions and plan their travel accordingly.

articles.full_text:
Nagarkurnool district has been placed under an orange alert from 8.30 am on November 2 to 8.30 am on November 3 as Cyclone Murasu is expected to bring heavy to very heavy rainfall, thunderstorms and strong winds of up to 60–90 kmph, according to the district administration.
District Collector Hemanta Keshav Patil has urged residents to follow advisories issued by the India Meteorological Department and take precautions during the alert period. The administration has also issued a yellow alert for November 3 and 4, indicating that weather-related risks are expected to continue after the orange-alert window ends.
Residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel while the warning is in force. The administration has specifically asked people to stay away from trees, electric poles and hoardings, which may become hazardous during strong winds. Residents have also been told to avoid open areas during lightning.
People living in low-lying areas have been asked to remain alert, as heavy rainfall can affect local movement and increase the risk of water accumulation. The advisory also asks residents to move livestock to safe locations during the period of adverse weather.
The warning has implications for road travel and access in areas vulnerable to heavy rain, while strong winds could create risks around overhead electrical infrastructure, roadside trees and temporary structures. The district administration has not provided details in the advisory about evacuations, road closures or damage-control measures.
Residents requiring emergency assistance can contact the Nagarkurnool district helpline at 9866756825. The administration has asked people to continue monitoring IMD advisories and follow official instructions during the orange and subsequent yellow-alert periods.

District Collector Hemanta Keshav Patil has urged residents to follow advisories issued by the India Meteorological Department and take necessary precautions during the alert period. Wind speeds are expected to reach between 60 kmph and 90 kmph, creating risks around trees, electric poles, hoardings and other exposed structures.
Residents have been advised to avoid unnecessary travel while the orange alert is in force. The administration has also asked people to stay away from trees, electric poles and hoardings, and to avoid open areas during lightning. These precautions are intended to reduce exposure to falling objects, electrical hazards and lightning-related incidents during periods of severe weather.
People living in low-lying areas have been asked to remain alert as heavy rainfall may affect local conditions. The district advisory also asks residents to keep livestock in safe places during the period of strong winds and intense rain.
The alert is part of a wider weather watch for the district. A yellow alert has been issued for November 3 and 4, indicating that residents will need to continue monitoring official updates after the orange-alert period ends. The administration has directed residents to rely on IMD advisories for information on changing weather conditions.
The warning also has implications for movement and basic services in areas exposed to rainfall, lightning and high winds. Avoiding unnecessary travel can help reduce risks on local roads, while staying clear of electric poles and hoardings is particularly important where weather conditions may weaken or dislodge structures. The advisory does not announce any specific road closures or service disruptions.
For emergencies, residents can contact the Nagarkurnool district helpline at 9866756825. The district administration has asked people to use the helpline when assistance is required and to continue following official safety instructions through the alert period.
